title: Review every change of the morning, and fix what it found
request: Review all fixes and changes I asked you to do in the last three hours.
spec: The owner's bug-finder rules: high-severity only, a concrete trigger for each, a minimal fix and a test.
plan: Four reviewers in parallel: the restyle, login and Home chat; prompt caching; the worker, the store job and own workspaces; the notebook cells again
Fix every finding with a test, then one gate

decisions.decision: Sign-in for make dev lives in .env.dev, read by make dev only.
decisions.why: The shared .env is read by make notebook, the flows and the tests, which refuse to start with sign-in and no database.

decisions.decision: A whole store run is queued only by the server's own workspace.
decisions.why: One run covers every workspace; each account's worker queuing its own multiplied the memory the worker died of.

decisions.decision: New data on a built project's chat starts a new chat; messages continue the old one.
decisions.why: A built project took its table at the build: data added to its chat could never reach it.

change: scripts/dev.py, .gitignore, Makefile, accounts/api.py, agentic/services.py, store/conductor.py, store/keepers/standard.py, models/prices.py, studio/kernels.py, routers/projects.py, the Home and Notebook pages, tests.

findings.defect: make login broke make notebook, the flows and serial tests.
findings.scenario: After make login the shared .env held DCLAB_AUTH=password and no database: every server but make dev's refused to start.
findings.cause: Sign-in was written to the file every entry point reads.
findings.fix: make dev's own file, .env.dev, read only by make dev.

findings.defect: make login took an empty or off sign-in as already on.
findings.scenario: A .env.dev with DCLAB_AUTH=none or DCLAB_AUTH= kept sign-in off while the command said it was on.
findings.cause: The check matched any value, and its whitespace ran past the line's end.
findings.fix: Only password or oidc counts; spaces within the line.

findings.defect: A workspace owner could place an existing account in a workspace they co-own.
findings.scenario: A friend who owns their lab added another user's email with their own workspace ticked: a lab was made around the victim with the friend as owner, and the victim's next sign-in landed there.
findings.cause: An existing account was used as found.
findings.fix: A workspace of their own is refused for an email that has an account (409).

findings.defect: A store run outlived its worker, with no timeout and the store's locks held.
findings.scenario: A code change restarted make dev's worker during a store job: the worker ended, its store process went on alone.
findings.cause: The worker was ended by its process only.
findings.fix: The worker runs in its own session and is ended with its whole group.

findings.defect: Each account's workspace queued a whole store run every hour.
findings.scenario: With N friends' labs, N store processes started in the same minute on the 8 GB machine.
findings.cause: The sweep ran in every workspace's worker, against one global schedule.
findings.fix: Only the server's own workspace queues it.

findings.defect: Cache writes were charged at the plain rate when a price had no cache rate.
findings.scenario: A prices file written before caching: an hour's cache write recorded at half its cost, and the caps' estimate too low.
findings.cause: The write premium applied only to prices with a cache read rate.
findings.fix: Writes always carry their premium; reads without a rate at the full price.

findings.defect: Coming back to Home replaced a chat in progress with the project's old chat.
findings.scenario: A new chat on Home, a visit to a project page, back to Home: the new chat was replaced and half-typed text would post into the built project's chat.
findings.cause: Home opened the current project's chat whenever it differed from the one on screen.
findings.fix: Home opens it only when no chat is on screen, checked again after the read.

findings.defect: Data added to a built project's chat went nowhere while the page said the project would change.
findings.scenario: Upload on a reopened built chat, then build: the old project opened, without the table.
findings.cause: A built project takes its table at the build.
findings.fix: New data on a built chat starts a new chat with the same problem, said in a toast; the note says how to change the project.

findings.defect: The kernel's copy of the training rows sat outside the project, kept by the store as content and left after a delete.
findings.scenario: A JSON table: the kernel's copy was not counted as a table, and deleting the project left it and its kernel.
findings.cause: The kernel's folder was under the workspace, not the project.
findings.fix: The folder is the project's kernel/data; delete stops the kernel and removes it.

findings.defect: A cell's printed rows and plots reached the store unshaped.
findings.scenario: An accepted cell printing frame.head(): its rows and its pictures were kept whole in the store.
findings.cause: Code runs were kept as they are, while notebooks' outputs are shaped.
findings.fix: The store keeps a cell's run as a notebook: printed tables out, pictures counted; the workspace's own file stays whole.

findings.defect: The Notebook page changed the project every page showed.
findings.scenario: A sample chosen on purpose elsewhere was replaced by the latest project on every page after one visit to Notebook.
findings.cause: The page wrote its choice into the shared state.
findings.fix: The page opens the latest project for itself only.

findings.defect: The kernel's fingerprint missed the pack.
findings.scenario: A pack changed without a new solution would keep the old strata's rows.
findings.cause: The pack picks the kind, and so the split.
findings.fix: The pack is part of the fingerprint.

findings.defect: My overwrite of an existing module, caught before commit.
findings.scenario: A new module written over dclab_core/evaluation.py, Phase 3's evaluation of answerers.
findings.cause: The name was not checked before writing.
findings.fix: The file restored from git; the new module is model_evaluation.py.
findings.test: git status clean on the restored file

measurements.name: Four reviews
measurements.result: 13 findings across the morning's changes, each fixed with a test or a browser check
limits: the reviewers read the code; the browser checks cover one project

outcome: The morning's changes reviewed and their findings fixed.
lessons: A setting written to the shared .env reaches every entry point that reads it, not only the one it was meant for.
A child process must die with its parent: start the parent in its own group and end the group.
Check a file name before writing a new module.
risks: Any signed-in member still runs code as the server's user until the sandbox step.
